summary: Connection hogging from aggressive client retry window serializes requests and causes tenant-wide perceived inference timeouts
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NoteAI reports a sudden increase in end-to-end inference latency and intermittent request timeouts starting 2026-03-10 22:00 UTC. The spikes appear tenant-scoped to their Dedicated pool. Symptoms are: long tail request latencies (95th+), repeated 504 errors from the API gateway, and a backlog of serialized requests visible in the gateway metrics.

Impact:
- NoteAI has several synchronous user-facing features degraded (document summarization and chat).
- Customer reports increased error rates and user complaints; business impact is high.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity (tenant: noteai-dedicated-01) in us-east-1
- SDK: noteai/sdk-js v2.3.1 (self-managed client integration)
- Serving: redwood-gpt-6b-v1 pinned

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Run a burst of short chat completion requests (avg tokens per request ~80) at 200 rps for tenant endpoints using the SDK with default config.
2) Observe gateway latencies climb and 504s returned after ~60s of sustained load.
3) Restarting the client recovers throughput for a short period before the pattern repeats.

Observed vs Expected:
- Observed: Long tail latencies, serialized request queue in gateway, upstream 504s, and apparent saturation despite available GPU capacity.
- Expected: Steady throughput at committed QPS with graceful backoff and no tenant-wide serialization.

Relevant logs and links:
- Customer-provided gateway traces (attached) and a short screen recording of metrics.
- Dashboard: https://console.redwood.company/dashboards/tenant/noteai-dedicated-01/latency (private)
- Support Slack thread: #support (link: slack://channel/support/p1623)
comments: 2026-03-11T10:05Z - Maya Thompson (Support): Acknowledged, creating ticket and requesting artifacts (gateway traces, client config). Escalated to SRE due to tenant-scoped impact.

2026-03-11T11:20Z - Liam Ortega (SRE): Initial triage: GPU utilization on dedicated pool is healthy. Observing large gradient in active connections and many long-lived keep-alive sockets from the customer's IP range. Asking for SDK config and sample traffic pattern.
2026-03-11T15:40Z - NoteAI (Customer): Provided sdk config (default retry/backoff), sample load generator script, and pcap of connections. We don't modify default retry behavior.

2026-03-12T09:12Z - Liam Ortega (SRE): Reproduced in lab with SDK v2.3.1: aggressive retry window combined with single-connection pooling resulted in request serialization at the gateway under intermittent transient errors. Raising to P1 and involving API-gateway owner.

2026-03-13T08:30Z - API Gateway Owner (Elena Park): Deployed temporary throttling for the tenant to limit concurrent inflight connections from single source. Observed reduction in serialized queue but some customer requests still hit 504 when SDK retries overlap with gateway timeouts.
2026-03-14T12:05Z - Liam Ortega (SRE): Rolling plan proposed: customer-side SDK config changes + server-side conn pool hardening. Need QA signoff before permanent changes.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-11: Confirmed dedicated GPU pool shows spare capacity; issue not due to model saturation.
2026-03-11: Gateway metrics show single-client connection counts spiking to >10k concurrent sockets; per-connection request queues growing disproportionately compared to other tenants.
2026-03-11: Packet captures show repeated client retries with short retry windows (0-100ms jitter) and no connection pool warm-up, causing many short-lived request bursts on the same connection.

2026-03-12: Reproduced locally using noteai/sdk-js v2.3.1 and default retry/backoff combined with maxSockets=1 in their custom HTTP agent; observed request serialization and cascading timeouts when one request hit a transient error and was retried aggressively.

2026-03-12: Hypothesis: Customer's HTTP agent configuration (single socket or very low maxSockets) + SDK aggressive immediate retry policy causes the client to queue requests behind a single connection or to reuse a connection in a way that serializes higher-level requests. When transient backend delays occur, retries flood the gateway while user requests wait serialized behind retries, producing perceived latency and timeouts.
2026-03-13: Experimented with increasing maxSockets and adding exponential backoff with jitter; result: dramatic reduction in serialized queue depth and lower 95th/99th percentiles in latency.
2026-03-13: Observed related errors in gateway: "upstream response timeout" and "request queue full" mapping to the tenant during incident windows.

2026-03-14: Identified SDK versions affected: noteai/sdk-js v2.2.x and v2.3.1 when used with custom Node HTTP agents that set maxSockets <=2 and default retry policy. Variants of the problem also present in some Python clients with urllib3 pool size forced to 1.

2026-03-14: Risk assessment: High for customers who adopted simplified client wrappers that centralize requests on a single pooled connection. Medium for default SDK configs but mitigatable via guidance.
2026-03-14: Linked historical tickets for context: SUP-30577 (connection-leak) and SUP-44107 (client-maxconns-sync-retries).
resolution:
Workaround applied (customer-side + server-side):
1) Customer applied immediate SDK mitigation: bumped HTTP agent maxSockets to 50 and enabled exponential backoff with randomized jitter; deployed within 2026-03-13 18:00 UTC. Customer reported near-immediate improvement in p95/p99 latencies and elimination of 504s.
2) Server-side: API gateway owners deployed a short-term per-connection request cap and extended idle keepalive timeout tuning for the tenant pool to reduce long-lived half-open connections.
3) Engineering follow-up: SDK team to publish a guidance note and add a warning in SDK docs about using low connection pool sizes with default aggressive retry settings.
4) Long-term fix: Platform will add telemetry-based tenant connection pattern alerts (SLO guardrails) and an automated mitigation that suggests per-tenant throttling or advising SDK config changes.

Post-action notes:
- Customer confirmed functional recovery and reduced error rates as of 2026-03-13 20:30 UTC.
- Owner: Liam Ortega (SRE) to track rollout of SDK documentation changes (target 2026-03-21).
- Follow-up task created for platform telemetry: INT-398 (track connection-pattern-alerts).
